notes.title: How the cuisine filters were policed
notes.body: Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. The region’s canon comes first: the Cuban sandwich and medianoche, croquetas, pastelitos and the ventanita cafecito, the frita, stone crab, Haitian griot, Peruvian ceviche, arepas, key lime pie, conch, Nicaraguan fritanga, Redland tropical fruit, and gator and frog legs at the Glades edge. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

notes.title: Web-searched, merit-measured and fact-checked
notes.body: Every place is traceable to at least two credible sources (or one institutional authority — Michelin, James Beard, the National Park Service) — the Miami Herald, Miami New Times, the Sun Sentinel, Eater Miami, The Infatuation, WLRN, Time Out, the Greater Miami and Fort Lauderdale tourism boards, Florida State Parks, Atlas Obscura and vetted creators — recorded in data/sources.json. Yelp, TripAdvisor and Google ratings never count as a recommender. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked.

places.ad: Royal Palm Visitor Center, State Road 9336, Everglades National Park, FL
places.w: The park's most popular trail: a paved path and boardwalk over sawgrass marsh and Taylor Slough where alligators, turtles and anhingas gather — best in the dry-season winter.
places.k: Walk it early morning Dec–Apr; watch for vultures on car rubber.

places.w: Everglades NP's northern entrance: a 15-mile paved loop through the river of grass to a 360° observation tower — by tram tour, bicycle or on foot.

places.ad: Main Park Road, Everglades National Park, FL
places.w: A short boardwalk to a raised platform with sweeping views over the sawgrass 'river of grass'.
The park's far southern end on Florida Bay: boat tours and rentals into the backcountry, crocodiles and manatees at the marina.

places.ad: 900 N Birch Rd, Fort Lauderdale, FL
places.w: The 1920s Caribbean-plantation-style waterfront estate of artists Frederic and Evelyn Bartlett, between the Intracoastal and the beach.

places.ad: Riverwalk, New River, Fort Lauderdale, FL
places.w: A brick promenade along the New River past mansions, the Stranahan House and riverside bars.
Built 1901 as Frank Stranahan's trading post — the oldest surviving structure in Broward County, now a museum.

places.n: Miami Beach Architectural District (Art Deco Historic District)
places.ad: Ocean Drive & Collins Ave, South Beach, Miami Beach, FL
places.w: The world's largest concentration of 1920s–30s Art Deco buildings, pastel hotels along Ocean Drive — on the National Register.
places.k: Walk Ocean Drive at dusk when the neon comes on.

places.w: Design museum and library in a restored 1927 storage building — 180,000 objects on how design shaped the modern world.
Morris Lapidus' 1960 pedestrian mall — a mile of cafés, shops and people-watching.
Waterfront park and pier at the tip of South Beach watching cruise ships slide out of Government Cut.
Kenneth Treister's 1990 memorial: a 42-ft bronze arm rising from a reflecting pool, ringed by figures and a granite wall of victims' names.
Miami Beach's contemporary art museum in a 1930s Deco building in Collins Park.
Downtown's 32-acre waterfront park on Biscayne Bay, with the Noguchi-designed amphitheatre and Challenger memorial.
PAMM — Miami's flagship contemporary art museum in a Herzog & de Meuron building with hanging gardens on the bay.

places.n: Phillip and Patricia Frost Museum of Science
places.w: Science museum, planetarium and a three-level aquarium with an oculus looking up into the Gulf Stream tank.
Tony Goldman's 2009 outdoor street-art museum that turned Wynwood's warehouses into the world's mural capital.
James Deering's 1916 Italian Renaissance–style villa and formal gardens on Biscayne Bay — Miami's grandest historic estate.

places.ad: 10901 Old Cutler Rd, Coral Gables, FL
places.w: 83 acres of palms, cycads and rare tropical plants — one of the country's great tropical botanical gardens.

places.n: Biscayne National Park — Dante Fascell Visitor Center
places.w: The mainland gateway to a park that is 95% water: museum, art gallery, ranger talks, and boat trips out to the keys, reefs and Stiltsville.

places.ad: Boca Chita Key, Biscayne National Park, FL
places.w: The park's most-visited island, greeted by the ornamental lighthouse Mark Honeywell built in the 1930s.

places.ad: Biscayne Bay off Cape Florida, Biscayne National Park, FL
places.w: The six surviving stilt houses standing in the shallows of Biscayne Bay since the 1930s — seen on guided boat tours.
Big Cypress National Preserve's main visitor centre on the Tamiami Trail — alligators line the canal out front.
A boardwalk into a cypress strand that ends at a gator hole where anhingas dry their wings.
The smallest post office in the United States — a 61-sq-ft former irrigation-pipe shed pressed into service after a 1953 fire.
places.k: Mail a postcard from it.

places.w: Miami-Dade's 37-acre Redland botanical park of 500+ edible tropical fruits, spices and nuts — taste what's in season.
Ed Leedskalnin's single-handed carved-coral monument (1923–51), still unexplained.
Since 1933: the humans walk in cages while the primates roam free.
Florida's oldest alligator farm (1940s) at the Everglades' edge — airboat rides and gator shows.
Key Biscayne's two-mile family beach with calm water, cabanas and beachside paella.

places.n: Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park
places.ad: 1200 S Crandon Blvd, Key Biscayne, FL
places.w: The tip of Key Biscayne: a mile of wild beach, nature trails and Miami-Dade's oldest structure, the 1825 Cape Florida Light.

places.ad: Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park, Key Biscayne, FL
places.w: The 1825 brick lighthouse — the oldest standing structure in Miami-Dade; climb it on ranger-led tours.
Opened in 1945 as the 'colored only' beach of segregated Miami; now a historic park on Virginia Key.
Wide family beach between Bal Harbour and Sunny Isles — kite flying since 1992, a skate park, and a clothing-optional section to the north.
1926 Mediterranean Revival grand hotel and South Florida's only National Historic Landmark resort.

places.ad: 2701 De Soto Blvd, Coral Gables, FL
places.w: A 1924 public pool carved from a coral-rock quarry — waterfalls, grottoes and Venetian bridges; on the National Register.
Coral Gables' downtown boulevard of shops, cafés and galleries.
University of Miami's art museum, home of the Kress Collection of Renaissance and Baroque art.

places.ad: SW 8th St, Little Havana, Miami, FL
places.w: The heart of Cuban Miami: cigar rollers, ventanitas, giant painted roosters and the Walk of Fame stars for Celia Cruz and Gloria Estefan.
A 1926 Art Deco cinema at Calle Ocho and 15th Ave, still screening films and hosting cultural events.
1925 Giralda-style tower built for the Miami News; 1962–74 the Cuban Refugee Center that processed ~300,000 exiles — the 'Ellis Island of the South'. National Historic Landmark (2008).
South Florida's history museum in the Cultural Plaza; it also manages the Miami Circle.
John Eberson's 1926 atmospheric movie palace for Paramount — stars twinkle on the ceiling; a Miami Film Festival venue.
A 2,000-year-old Tequesta circle of 24 post-holes cut into limestone at the mouth of the Miami River, found in 1998. National Historic Landmark.
Overtown's 1913 theatre at the heart of 'Little Broadway', where Count Basie, Billie Holiday and Aretha Franklin played; now the Black Archives' home.

places.ad: 16711 W Dixie Hwy, North Miami Beach, FL
places.w: A 12th-century Cistercian cloister from Segovia, bought by William Randolph Hearst, shipped in crates and reassembled in North Miami Beach.

places.ad: 3400 NE 163rd St, North Miami Beach, FL
places.w: Florida's largest urban park: 1,000+ acres of mangrove estuary with kayaking, paddleboarding and 15 miles of mountain-bike trails.

places.n: Museum of Contemporary Art North Miami (MOCA)
places.w: Contemporary art museum with ~500 works and free last-Friday Jazz at MOCA concerts.
A natural limestone bridge over Arch Creek, Tequesta archaeological site and nature centre.

places.ad: 17530 W Dixie Hwy, North Miami Beach, FL
places.w: 1930s county park with a rock-built 'castle' mound, a rookery and a 1964 nine-hole course.
One of the largest private contemporary-art collections in the world (7,200+ works), in Allapattah — with two Kusama Infinity Mirror Rooms.

places.n: Institute of Contemporary Art, Miami (ICA Miami)
places.w: Free contemporary art museum in the Design District, with a sculpture garden.
The world's first museum dedicated to graffiti art, in Wynwood.
Luxury flagships threaded with serious public art and architecture — Buckminster Fuller's Fly's Eye Dome, the Le Corbusier-inspired garage.
A 2½-mile 1950s-flavoured beachfront promenade of mom-and-pop shops and ice-cream parlours, with free music at the Hollywood Beach Theatre.

places.ad: 3109 E Sunrise Blvd, Fort Lauderdale, FL
places.w: 180 acres of Old Florida hammock and mangrove between the ocean and the Intracoastal — paddling, trails, picnic lawns.
200+ hands-on exhibits, live-animal habitats and a five-storey IMAX on the Riverwalk.
60-acre botanical garden and wildlife sanctuary with some of Florida's largest, oldest trees and a 1930s house museum.

places.ad: 3600 W Sample Rd, Coconut Creek, FL
places.w: The 'Butterfly Capital of the World': 20,000 butterflies and birds in screened aviaries and gardens.
The only subtropical zoo in the continental US — 2,000+ animals in open, moated habitats.
Charles Deering's 1920s bayfront estate with what's believed to be the largest old-growth coastal tropical hardwood hammock in the continental US — nature walks, boat trips, night hikes.

places.ad: 9610 Old Cutler Rd, Coral Gables, FL
places.w: County park whose man-made atoll pool is refreshed by Biscayne Bay's tides.
Bayside county park and marina next to Biscayne NP's visitor centre, on land donated in 1938.
N.B.T. Roney's 1925 'historic Spanish village' — two pink-stucco, tile-roofed blocks of cafés under striped awnings.

places.ad: 2000 Convention Center Dr, Miami Beach, FL
places.w: 4.5 acres of orchids, a Japanese garden and a living wall beside the Convention Center — free.
Florida Jewish history since 1763, housed in two restored former synagogues in South of Fifth.
Plant explorer David Fairchild's nine-acre Coconut Grove estate, now a National Tropical Botanical Garden; tours by reservation.
The 1891 home of Commodore Ralph Munroe — the oldest house in Miami still on its original site, on a waterfront lawn that hosts bluegrass and folk nights.
Coconut Grove's renovated open-air shopping and dining centre.
Virginia Key's marine park (1955) permanently closed on 12 October 2025 after 70 years; a replacement aquarium is planned for ~2030.

pv.ss: Closed permanently 12 Oct 2025 after 70 years — Local10/WIBW; TimeOut Miami 2025-10-15, WLRN 2025-10-16, The Miami Hurricane 2025-10-14

places.w: 1925 racetrack on the National Register — 200 acres of royal palms, a casino, quarter-horse racing and its famous Audubon-sanctuary colony of pink flamingos.
Glenn Curtiss's 1926 Arabian Nights city: the domed, minaretted Moorish Revival city hall is the starting point for a tour of ~90 Moorish buildings.

places.ad: 347 Don Shula Dr, Miami Gardens, FL
places.w: Home of the Miami Dolphins and the Hurricanes; Super Bowl LIV and the Miami Grand Prix circuit.
One of America's largest malls, with a public art programme — Carsten Höller's 93-ft spiral Aventura Slide Tower is a rideable sculpture.

places.n: Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts
places.w: Miami's $500M César Pelli performing-arts centre — Broadway, opera, ballet and the Art Deco Sears tower preserved on its plaza.
Bayfront home arena of the Miami Heat and the city's big-concert stage.
Free elevated people-mover with 21 stations — the best (and cheapest) skyline ride through downtown and Brickell.
Small man-made island off Brickell with a waterfront perimeter path — the neighbourhood's quiet escape.

places.ad: Under the Metrorail, Brickell, Miami, FL
places.w: Linear park and trail being built beneath the Metrorail — the Brickell Backyard section has gyms, gardens and the Oolite Room.

places.n: Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino (Guitar Hotel)
places.w: The Seminole Tribe's 450-foot guitar-shaped hotel tower, casino and Hard Rock Live arena — Broward's most improbable landmark.
Broward's north-end beach with the International Fishing Pier and a laid-back boardwalk.
Wide beach with the rebuilt Fisher Family Pier and some of Broward's best shore diving and fishing.
Quiet barrier-island beach beneath the 1907 Hillsboro Inlet lighthouse, one of the most powerful on the East Coast.
Old-Florida beach town with a fishing pier and quiet sand between Port Everglades and Hollywood.
A 1920s industrial bakery turned (since 1985) into ~100 artists' studios and galleries — open studios show Wynwood before the murals.

places.ad: Everglades National Park (Long Pine Key area), FL
places.w: Cold War Nike Hercules 'Alpha Battery' frozen since 1979 — barracks, missile barns and a real missile; ranger-led tours in season.

places.ad: Royal Palm, Everglades National Park, FL
places.w: Shaded, jungle-like paved loop through a hardwood hammock beside the Anhinga Trail at Royal Palm.

places.ad: 815 Oyster Bar Ln, Everglades City, FL
places.w: The park's western gateway — boat tours into the Ten Thousand Islands mangrove maze and backcountry paddling routes.
Largest island of Biscayne NP — a former pioneer pineapple-farming and sponging community; camping, a loop trail, bayside picnics (check NPS for current access).
Day-use island on swift Caesar Creek with a short hardwood-hammock trail, picnic pavilion and dawn-to-dusk access.

places.ad: Tamiami Trail & Turner River Rd, Ochopee, FL
places.w: 200-m boardwalk over a cypress waterway packed with gators, turtles and wading birds — the gateway to Turner River Road.

places.ad: Turner River Rd (CR 839), Big Cypress National Preserve, FL
places.w: 17-mile gravel loop through wet prairies and cypress — one of South Florida's best drive-up gator and wading-bird routes.

places.ad: Ocean Dr, 5th–15th St, Miami Beach, FL
places.w: The classic South Beach strand in front of Ocean Drive's Art Deco row — lifeguard towers, volleyball, the people-watching beach.
Sidewalk stars honouring Latin stars from Celia Cruz to Gloria Estefan along Calle Ocho.
1917 stilt-built trading post and post office at the end of the road on Chokoloskee — now a museum of frontier and Seminole trade (NRHP).
Collier County museum in the 1927 Everglades Laundry — Calusa, Seminole, pioneer and Barron Collier history of the southwest Glades.
Home of Dana A. Dorsey, Florida's first Black millionaire, who built Overtown one rental house per parcel — NRHP-listed (1989).

places.ad: SW 152nd St (across from Zoo Miami), Miami, FL
places.w: 50-acre rail museum across from Zoo Miami — home of the Ferdinand Magellan, the armoured presidential Pullman used by FDR, Truman, Eisenhower and Reagan; train rides and Florida's largest public model railroad.
'Living' aviation museum at the Kendall-Tamiami airport — warbirds that still fly, including a B-26 from the Bay of Pigs invasion.
The original 1936 Parrot Jungle site, now a municipal botanical garden — strangler figs, cypress slough, koi, Swan Lake and the old jungle trails.

places.ad: Hialeah, FL (unincorporated Miami-Dade, north of Hialeah)
places.w: 515-acre Hialeah park on the old naval air station Earhart flew from — five lakes, the Miami Watersports Complex wakeboard cable, farm village and mountain-bike trails.
Open-air waterfront market on Biscayne Bay — live music daily, bay-cruise docks and the downtown skyline.
18-acre tropical zoological park on Watson Island — the successor to Parrot Jungle, with sloths, lemurs, flamingos and macaws.
Haitian arts centre with galleries, a 300-seat theatre, the Saturday Caribbean Marketplace and the monthly Big Night in Little Haiti Kreyòl concerts.

places.ad: Las Olas Blvd, Fort Lauderdale, FL
places.w: Broward's flagship art museum on Las Olas — 7,500+ works incl. the largest US collection of CoBrA art and William Glackens; free first Thursdays.
10-acre turn-of-the-century railroad workers' village in Goulds — tropical gardens, antique shops, galleries, tearoom and an aviary.
County marina on Biscayne Bay — gateway to Biscayne NP's keys, with the Biscayne Trail loop and a 1.5-mile jetty walk.
270 acres of pineland next to Zoo Miami — the county's biggest campground, a swimming lake with a seasonal beach and water slide, bridle trails.
Miami's oldest institution still on its original site — the 1924 Mediterranean Revival Jesuit church designed by Owen Williams of Palm Beach.

places.ad: 1821 SW 9th St, Little Havana, Miami, FL
places.w: Veterans' museum of the 1961 invasion — its prize is the Brigade 2506 flag JFK held up at the Orange Bowl in 1962.

places.n: American Museum of the Cuban Diaspora
places.w: 'The Cuban' — exhibitions on the exile experience and Cuban-American art, in a 1930s Coral Way building.
Two decades of Haitian art, artifacts, music and film in the Design District.

places.ad: 17th St (Lincoln Road area), Miami Beach, FL
places.w: Frank Gehry's home for the New World Symphony — free WALLCAST concerts and SoundScape Cinema projected on the façade over the park lawn.

places.ad: Ocean Dr at 11th St, Miami Beach, FL
places.w: The 1930 Mediterranean mansion Gianni Versace made famous — now a hotel and restaurant on Ocean Drive.

places.n: Dr. Von D. Mizell-Eula Johnson State Park
places.w: 310-acre barrier-island park (formerly John U. Lloyd) named for the civil-rights leaders who desegregated Broward's beaches — Whiskey Creek paddling, nature trails, beach.
Broward's Everglades airboat park where Animal Planet's 'Gator Boys' was filmed — airboat rides and gator shows.
Morris Lapidus's 1954 MiMo icon — the curving tower, bow-tie floors and the famous 'Staircase to Nowhere'.
Miami's only Art Deco skyscraper (1939) — black-granite base and a lavish lobby with bronze elevator doors of egrets, herons and ibises.
Schultze & Weaver's 1927 Flagler-era office tower — Florentine eaves, bronze doors and a hand-painted lobby ceiling.
8-acre bayfront park among Edgewater's towers — waterfront promenade, courts and a dog park.
George Merrick's boyhood home — the 1899 family cottage grown into the coral-rock house where Coral Gables was dreamed up; tours on weekends.
The city's oldest public building (1923–24) — Richard Kiehnel's Spanish Colonial Revival church on land Merrick gave in his father's memory.

places.ad: 3429 Devon Rd (at Main Hwy), Coconut Grove, FL
places.w: 1917 coral-rock mission church hand-built by Felix Rebom with a hatchet, trowel, plumb line and T-square; the congregation dates to 1897.

places.ad: Washington Ave, South Beach, Miami Beach, FL
places.w: Howard Lovewell Cheney's 1937 'Deco Federal' rotunda with Charles Hardman's 1940 New Deal murals of Ponce de León and de Soto.
Miami's only two-Michelin-star restaurant (2026 Florida guide): Robuchon's counter-dining format in the Design District.
